tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 1
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A resin kiln uses the calibration $M(s)=5s^{3}$ for block mass. The log entry at $s=4$ reports $320$ grams.
A polymer printer obeys the power law $M(s)=Ks^{3}$. Doubling the mold length is said to multiply material use by $9$.
A tank obeys $2h^{3}=250$ at its target fill. An operator proposes the positive depth $5$.
A packaging scanner squares a reading with $g(x)=x^2$ before applying $f(u)=2u^{3/2}$. For an entry of $3$, the controller is claimed to return $36$.
A sheet-metal shop has area law $A=kr^2$. Increasing every radius by $20\%$ is claimed to increase area by $44\%$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Substitute the recorded input into the stated model:

$$M(4)=5(4)^3$$

Interpret the rational or negative exponent before doing the final arithmetic:

$$M(4)=5\cdot64$$

Hence the model output is

$$M(4)=320\text{ grams}$$

The stem's value is $320\text{ grams}$, so the numerical comparison is

$$320=320$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Form a ratio so the unknown positive coefficient and the original input cancel:

$$\frac{M(2s)}{M(s)}
=\frac{K(2s)^{3}}{Ks^{3}}$$

Separate the scale factor from the original power:

$$\frac{M(2s)}{M(s)}
=(2)^{3}$$

Evaluating that power gives

$$(2)^{3}=8$$

The proposed multiplier is $9$, and therefore

$$8\ne9$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Keep the positive-domain restriction in view and isolate the power first:

$$2h^{3}=250$$

Divide by the coefficient:

$$h^{3}=125$$

Raise both sides to the reciprocal exponent:

$$h=(125)^{\frac{1}{3}}=5$$

Only the positive solution is admissible in this model. Comparing it with the proposed value gives

$$5=5$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Composition is ordered: evaluate the inner map before the outer map.

$$g(3)=3^2=9$$

Insert that inner output into $f$:

$$f(g(3))=2(9)^{3/2}$$

Complete the power evaluation:

$$2\cdot27=54$$

The displayed claim is $36$, so

$$54\ne36$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Convert the input percentage change to the exact multiplier $\dfrac{6}{5}$ and apply the power exponent:

$$\frac{Y_{\rm new}}{Y_{\rm old}}
=(\dfrac{6}{5})^{2}=\dfrac{36}{25}$$

Translate the output multiplier back to a percentage increase:

$$\left|\dfrac{36}{25}-1\right|\cdot100\%=44\%$$

The direction follows from the multiplier being above $1$:

$$\frac{Y_{\rm new}}{Y_{\rm old}}>1$$

The stem gives $44\%$, so the decisive comparison is

$$44\%=44\%$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 2
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: For a lighthouse lens, $B(d)=Kd^{1/2}$ links aperture to beam width. Increasing the aperture ninefold allegedly scales the width by $3$.
A factory must satisfy $12L^{\frac{1}{2}}=60$ to meet its quota. The staffing plan sets $L=26$.
A chemical monitor first uses $g(x)=8x^3$, then compresses the result through $f(u)=\frac12u^{1/3}$. Its display at $x=4$ is said to be $4$.
An online market models demand as $q(p)=Kp^{-1.4}$. Its analyst reports a constant price elasticity of $\dfrac{-7}{10}$.
Before a theatre opens, its lighting console predicts beam width with $B(d)=12d^{1/2}$. A technician says the setting $d=81$ produces a width of $109$ units.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Form a ratio so the unknown positive coefficient and the original input cancel:

$$\frac{B(9d)}{B(d)}
=\frac{K(9d)^{\frac{1}{2}}}{Kd^{\frac{1}{2}}}$$

Separate the scale factor from the original power:

$$\frac{B(9d)}{B(d)}
=(9)^{\frac{1}{2}}$$

Evaluating that power gives

$$(9)^{\frac{1}{2}}=3$$

The proposed multiplier is $3$, and therefore

$$3=3$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Keep the positive-domain restriction in view and isolate the power first:

$$12L^{\frac{1}{2}}=60$$

Divide by the coefficient:

$$L^{\frac{1}{2}}=5$$

Raise both sides to the reciprocal exponent:

$$L=(5)^{2}=25$$

Only the positive solution is admissible in this model. Comparing it with the proposed value gives

$$25\ne26$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Composition is ordered: evaluate the inner map before the outer map.

$$g(4)=8(4)^3=512$$

Insert that inner output into $f$:

$$f(g(4))=\frac12(512)^{1/3}$$

Complete the power evaluation:

$$\frac12\cdot8=4$$

The displayed claim is $4$, so

$$4=4$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

For a power law $Y=Kx^a$, differentiate before forming elasticity:

$$\frac{dY}{dx}=Ka x^{a-1}$$

Use the point-elasticity definition:

$$\varepsilon=\frac{x}{Y}\frac{dY}{dx}
=\frac{x}{Kx^a}\left(Ka x^{a-1}\right)$$

All variable and coefficient factors cancel:

$$\varepsilon=a=\dfrac{-7}{5}$$

The reported elasticity is $\dfrac{-7}{10}$, and hence

$$\dfrac{-7}{5}\ne\dfrac{-7}{10}$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → False

Substitute the recorded input into the stated model:

$$B(81)=12\sqrt{81}$$

Interpret the rational or negative exponent before doing the final arithmetic:

$$B(81)=12\cdot9$$

Hence the model output is

$$B(81)=108\text{ units}$$

The stem's value is $109\text{ units}$, so the numerical comparison is

$$108\ne109$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

statements: A beacon's target signal imposes $96d^{-2}=6$. Its installation guide recommends $d=4$.

A rescue beacon estimates received intensity through $I(d)=96d^{-2}$. At the documented separation $d=4$, the manual lists an intensity of $6$ lux.

tactical_explanations:
**A.** → True

Keep the positive-domain restriction in view and isolate the power first:

$$96d^{-2}=6$$

Divide by the coefficient:

$$d^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{16}$$

Raise both sides to the reciprocal exponent:

$$d=(\dfrac{1}{16})^{\frac{-1}{2}}=4$$

$$4=4$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**B.** → False

Composition is ordered: evaluate the inner map before the outer map.

$$g(5)=16(5)^2=400$$

Insert that inner output into $f$:

$$f(g(5))=\sqrt{400}$$

Complete the power evaluation:

$$\sqrt{400}=20$$

The displayed claim is $25$, so

$$20\ne25$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Rewrite the rational or negative power in ordinary real terms:

$$x^{1/2}=\sqrt{x}$$

This reveals the admissible inputs and attainable outputs:

$$x\ge0,\qquad R=6\sqrt{x}\ge0$$

Therefore the actual domain-range pair is

$$x\ge0\text{ and }R\ge0$$

The report states $x\ge0\text{ and }R\ge0$, so

$$x\ge0\text{ and }R\ge0=x\ge0\text{ and }R\ge0$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → True

Substitute the recorded input into the stated model:

$$I(4)=\frac{96}{4^2}$$

Interpret the rational or negative exponent before doing the final arithmetic:

$$I(4)=\frac{96}{16}$$

Hence the model output is

$$I(4)=6\text{ lux}$$

The stem's value is $6\text{ lux}$, so the numerical comparison is

$$6=6$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

Form a ratio so the unknown positive coefficient and the original input cancel:

$$\frac{I(3d)}{I(d)}
=\frac{K(3d)^{-2}}{Kd^{-2}}$$

Separate the scale factor from the original power:

$$\frac{I(3d)}{I(d)}
=(3)^{-2}$$

Evaluating that power gives

$$(3)^{-2}=\dfrac{1}{9}$$

The proposed multiplier is $\dfrac{10}{9}$, and therefore

$$\dfrac{1}{9}\ne\dfrac{10}{9}$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

statements: A growth simulator applies $g(x)=x^3$ and then $f(u)=6u^{2/3}$. The scenario $x=3$ is labelled with output $162$.
A detector obeys the inverse-square law $I=kd^{-2}$. A $25\%$ rise in distance is claimed to lower intensity by $36\%$.
A diving chamber computes pressure from $P(v)=15v^{-1}$. The gauge reading corresponding to $v=5$ is asserted to be $3$ bar.
A sonar array follows $F(d)=Kd^{-3}$ for echo force. Doubling range is described as retaining $\dfrac{9}{8}$ of the original force.
An energy store must solve $2x^{\frac{5}{2}}=486$. The control room enters the positive setting $9$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

Composition is ordered: evaluate the inner map before the outer map.

$$g(3)=3^3=27$$

Insert that inner output into $f$:

$$f(g(3))=6(27)^{2/3}$$

Complete the power evaluation:

$$6\cdot9=54$$

The displayed claim is $162$, so

$$54\ne162$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → True

Convert the input percentage change to the exact multiplier $\dfrac{5}{4}$ and apply the power exponent:

$$\frac{Y_{\rm new}}{Y_{\rm old}}
=(\dfrac{5}{4})^{-2}=\dfrac{16}{25}$$

Translate the output multiplier back to a percentage decrease:

$$\left|\dfrac{16}{25}-1\right|\cdot100\%=36\%$$

The direction follows from the multiplier being below $1$:

$$\frac{Y_{\rm new}}{Y_{\rm old}}<1$$

The stem gives $36\%$, so the decisive comparison is

$$36\%=36\%$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**C.** → True

Substitute the recorded input into the stated model:

$$P(5)=\frac{15}{5}$$

Interpret the rational or negative exponent before doing the final arithmetic:

$$P(5)=15\div5$$

Hence the model output is

$$P(5)=3\text{ bar}$$

The stem's value is $3\text{ bar}$, so the numerical comparison is

$$3=3$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Form a ratio so the unknown positive coefficient and the original input cancel:

$$\frac{F(2d)}{F(d)}
=\frac{K(2d)^{-3}}{Kd^{-3}}$$

Separate the scale factor from the original power:

$$\frac{F(2d)}{F(d)}
=(2)^{-3}$$

Evaluating that power gives

$$(2)^{-3}=\dfrac{1}{8}$$

The proposed multiplier is $\dfrac{9}{8}$, and therefore

$$\dfrac{1}{8}\ne\dfrac{9}{8}$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Keep the positive-domain restriction in view and isolate the power first:

$$2x^{\frac{5}{2}}=486$$

Divide by the coefficient:

$$x^{\frac{5}{2}}=243$$

Raise both sides to the reciprocal exponent:

$$x=(243)^{\frac{2}{5}}=9$$

Only the positive solution is admissible in this model. Comparing it with the proposed value gives

$$9=9$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

tasks.title: Exam-style tasks - 10
tasks.context: Evaluate each statement. Mark it TRUE or FALSE.
statements: A streaming platform predicts load with $L(n)=Kn^{1.25}$. The model team gives its user elasticity as $\dfrac{4}{5}$.
A composite workshop predicts stress with $S(a)=4a^{3/4}$. Its certificate assigns $33$ units when $a=16$.
A circular coating process has $A(r)=Kr^{2}$. Enlarging radius by the factor $\frac32$ is claimed to scale coating demand by $\dfrac{9}{4}$.
A signal tower reaches calibration at $9t^{\frac{4}{3}}=144$. Its technician chooses $t=9$.
A geometry tool sends $x$ through $g(x)=25x^2$ and afterward through $f(u)=2u^{1/2}$. At $x=4$, the final panel shows $40$.
tactical_explanations:
**A.** → False

For a power law $Y=Kx^a$, differentiate before forming elasticity:

$$\frac{dY}{dx}=Ka x^{a-1}$$

Use the point-elasticity definition:

$$\varepsilon=\frac{x}{Y}\frac{dY}{dx}
=\frac{x}{Kx^a}\left(Ka x^{a-1}\right)$$

All variable and coefficient factors cancel:

$$\varepsilon=a=\dfrac{5}{4}$$

The reported elasticity is $\dfrac{4}{5}$, and hence

$$\dfrac{5}{4}\ne\dfrac{4}{5}$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**B.** → False

Substitute the recorded input into the stated model:

$$S(16)=4(\sqrt[4]{16})^3$$

Interpret the rational or negative exponent before doing the final arithmetic:

$$S(16)=4\cdot8$$

Hence the model output is

$$S(16)=32\text{ units}$$

The stem's value is $33\text{ units}$, so the numerical comparison is

$$32\ne33$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**C.** → True

Form a ratio so the unknown positive coefficient and the original input cancel:

$$\frac{A(\dfrac{3}{2}r)}{A(r)}
=\frac{K(\dfrac{3}{2}r)^{2}}{Kr^{2}}$$

Separate the scale factor from the original power:

$$\frac{A(\dfrac{3}{2}r)}{A(r)}
=(\dfrac{3}{2})^{2}$$

Evaluating that power gives

$$(\dfrac{3}{2})^{2}=\dfrac{9}{4}$$

The proposed multiplier is $\dfrac{9}{4}$, and therefore

$$\dfrac{9}{4}=\dfrac{9}{4}$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.

**D.** → False

Keep the positive-domain restriction in view and isolate the power first:

$$9t^{\frac{4}{3}}=144$$

Divide by the coefficient:

$$t^{\frac{4}{3}}=16$$

Raise both sides to the reciprocal exponent:

$$t=(16)^{\frac{3}{4}}=8$$

Only the positive solution is admissible in this model. Comparing it with the proposed value gives

$$8\ne9$$

The mathematical result does not agree with the claim, so the statement is False.

**E.** → True

Composition is ordered: evaluate the inner map before the outer map.

$$g(4)=25(4)^2=400$$

Insert that inner output into $f$:

$$f(g(4))=2\sqrt{400}$$

Complete the power evaluation:

$$2\cdot20=40$$

The displayed claim is $40$, so

$$40=40$$

The mathematical result agrees with the claim, so the statement is True.
